key_points: HP warned that global PC unit volumes will decline mid-single digits in 2027, a forward-looking demand signal that challenges the recent AI-PC driven rally narrative.
Morgan Stanley flagged that unit and margin pressures are not priced into HP's multi-year valuation highs, suggesting the stock may be vulnerable to downward revisions.
HP is holding off on fiscal 2027 guidance, creating near-term uncertainty and limiting visibility for investors.
Rising costs compound the demand headwind, pressuring margins at a time when revenue growth is expected to slow.
Despite the pullback, HP trades near its 52-week range highs with AI server/AI-PC catalysts still intact, so the risk is more of a valuation reset than a structural collapse.
